awd_titl_txt: Conference: Advances and Connections of Modern Geometric Function Theory
awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports the "Conference: Advances and Connections of Modern Geometric Function Theory", which will be held at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, October 25-26, 2025. Geometric function theory is a core subfield of mathematical analysis, and it has deep applications in many scientific fields, including physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, material science, and computer science. This conference will feature presentations from both leading experts and rising stars in the field and is designed to enhance the education of as well as foster collaboration among the participants. This will contribute to the training of the next generation of mathematicians and also help enhance the pre-eminent position of the US at the forefront of geometric function theory. In addition to plenary talks, the program includes short talks, a poster session, and an open problem session. The wide and varied array of conference participants will allow for exceptional exchanges of ideas between early-career and more established mathematicians.  More information can be found on the conference website https://lsa.umich.edu/math/seminars/conference-on-advances-and-connections-of-modern-geometric-funct.html.
 

Over the last few decades, the impact of geometric function theory is now seen in many fields including analysis on metric spaces, mappings of finite distortion, conformal geometry, nonlinear PDE, and geometric group theory. The presentations will focus on practical applications of techniques originated in geometric function theory. The mathematics discussed will address challenges within the related fields mentioned above, as well as the reciprocal influence of these areas on geometric function theory. This collaborative spirit aims to foster deeper exploration and innovation within the mathematical community to advance research in modern geometric function theory and related areas.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project, the Conference on Advances and Connections of Modern Geometric Function Theory, held at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, October 24-26, 2025, attracted more than 50 participants across the world. About half of the participants are early career faculty members, post docs, or graduate students.

Analysis plays a fundamental role in mathematics, and it has deep applications in numerous scientific fields, including physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, material sciences and computer sciences. Over the last few decades, geometric function theory - a subfield in analysis and a major focus of this conference, has broadened its scope, interactions and connections with many research areas including, but not limited to, analysis on metric spaces, mappings of finite distortion, conformal geometry and nonlinear PDE, and geometric group theory.

This conference gathered leading experts in the field from around the world and a significant number of postdocs and graduate students from the US to share their views on the current state of the art and collaborate on addressing the most important questions in the subject. The 16 talks and 8 poster presentations showcased a broad range of new findings as well as interesting open problems on the practical applications of techniques originated in geometric function theory in addressing challenges within related fields mentioned above, as well as the reciprocal influence of these areas on geometric function theory. Through the talks, poster presentations, and discussion sessions, participants of various career stages actively engaged in exchanging ideas, enhancing on-going collaborations, and forging new collaborations. This particularly benefits the participating graduate students who just entered the field or are considering entering.

By providing such a platform to exchange ideas and foster collaborations, this project will contribute to the advancement of sciences and the education of the next generation of scientists. It will also help maintain and enhance the leading position of the US in the field of analysis.
